episode_title: #135 Jennifer Davis, Tech Entrepreneur and Business Titan, Running for Congress!

real_qa.q: What problem did Davisware solve for HVAC and trade service industries?
real_qa.r: Davisware solved the core logistical challenge in the trades: getting the right person to the right place at the right time with the right parts and skills. They built dispatch board software integrated with billing, inventory, GPS, accounting, and CPA-compliant systems with 30 modules total. Their predictive analytics matched technician skillsets and likely parts to customer problems, enabling first-time fixes and reducing truck inventory by 50% while improving staff efficiency from 1-to-1 office-to-field ratios down to 3-to-1 or 4-to-1.
real_qa.requete: What did Davisware software do for HVAC companies

real_qa.q: How much did Davisware cost annually and what were the cost savings?
real_qa.r: Davisware pricing switched to a SaaS model costing approximately $7,000 to $8,000 per month for a mid-sized HVAC company. Previously, customers paid $150,000 to $200,000 to purchase the software outright plus 18% to 22% annual maintenance. The software delivered hundreds of thousands of dollars in annual savings through reducing on-board parts inventory by 50%, cutting back-office labor from 1-to-1 to 3-to-1 or 4-to-1 ratios, and enabling technicians to add direct revenue opportunities.

real_qa.q: When did Jennifer Davis and her husband start Davisware and what was their first revenue?
real_qa.r: Jennifer Davis and her husband Dan started Davisware in 1988 when she was 17 years old while both were in college—she at the University of Wisconsin studying elementary education, he at the University of Chicago studying math. They spent the summer trying to solve technology problems in Dan's brother's heating and air conditioning business. By ages 19 to 20, the business was under one million dollars in revenue.

real_qa.q: What were the three main industries that Davisware focused on besides HVAC?
real_qa.r: Beyond commercial HVAC, Davisware focused on commercial food equipment service (companies servicing restaurants) and petroleum equipment service (companies servicing gas stations). All three industries shared the common denominator of parts with serial numbers that were complicated and often regulated—making mistakes in food service could sicken people, and mistakes at gas stations could cause explosions.
real_qa.requete: Davisware industries food equipment petroleum HVAC

real_qa.q: When did Jennifer Davis sell Davisware and to whom?
real_qa.r: Jennifer Davis sold Davisware to Sarent Capital in July 2019, becoming a minority investor. She remained in an operating role until January 2023, then stayed on the board until April 2025 when Sarent Capital sold the company to ECI, a Dallas-based field service software company that continues to service the same industries.

guest.bio_context: Jennifer Davis grew up as the sixth of nine children on a farm in rural Wisconsin. She met her husband Dan at age 17 on Lake Grapevine in Dallas, Texas, and together they founded Davisware while still in college in 1988 to solve technology problems in the heating and air conditioning industry. She sold Davisware to Sarent Capital in July 2019, remained in an operating role until January 2023, and stayed on the board until April 2025 when the company was sold to ECI. She is now running for the eighth congressional seat in Illinois.
